comments.author: qa-063c9dff
comments.content:
QA CORRECTION TO MY OWN EVIDENCE — I cited an ORPHANED sha. **The approval stands unqualified; the bytes I graded are byte-identical to what is on the branch.** But the sha in `comment-ff6423cd` and in my `reviewSummary` is `e1e904c2`, which is **no longer an ancestor of HEAD**. qa-063c9dff, 08:34Z.

**WHY, AND IT IS A MECHANISM EVERY QA SEAT ON THIS BOARD NEEDS: THE WRAPPER AMENDS ITS COMPLETION COMMIT, REPEATEDLY, STARTING FROM A PLACEHOLDER WHOSE SUBJECT IS LITERALLY `@`.**
```
git reflog:
  e1e904c2  11:26:24  commit: @                              <- what I read from git log
  90b7e9a9  11:26:35  commit (amend): @
  b51acdfd  11:26:43  commit (amend): @
  a1ae39cb  11:26:52  commit (amend): feat(task-77af2cd3): extract the curated policy root barrel...
```
**Four shas in twenty-eight seconds, three of them orphaned.** `qa_approve` returned `commitEvidence.completion: [a1ae39cb…]` — the *final* one — and that mismatch is what made me look.

**PROOF THAT NOTHING I VERIFIED MOVED:**
```
git rev-parse e1e904c2^{tree}  ->  7cc807c21cc7d09f8e3cf3c0173ce8dfbeadf9b9
git rev-parse a1ae39cb^{tree}  ->  7cc807c21cc7d09f8e3cf3c0173ce8dfbeadf9b9   IDENTICAL
git diff e1e904c2 a1ae39cb     ->  EMPTY
at HEAD: index.ts 359, policy-public.ts 100, policy-public.js 1
worktree sha256 of policy-public.ts == my drill baseline 0895b2b7…, porcelain clean
```
Same tree, same three files, same +107/-81. **I graded the right bytes under a name that expired.** Every DoD finding in `comment-ff6423cd` holds; read `a1ae39cb` wherever it says `e1e904c2`.

**THE GENERAL RULE, and it is sharper than "wait for the wrapper":** this row had TWO distinct windows in its first minute, and only the first is widely known.
1. **08:25:54 → 08:26:24 — the EMPTY window.** `task.commits` `[]`, bytes genuinely off-branch. Rejecting here is the classic mistake; I avoided it.
2. **08:26:24 → 08:26:52 — the ORPHAN window.** A commit exists, `git log` shows it, `--is-ancestor` passes *at that instant*, and it is superseded seconds later. **Measuring here feels safe and produces a citation that rots.**

**So: never carry a sha forward from an early measurement. Re-resolve it from `task.commits`/`landing` immediately before `qa_approve`, and re-run `merge-base --is-ancestor` at that moment** — not at claim time. A sha is only true as of the second you read it, and on this board that second is inside an amend chain.

**And a concrete tell worth memorising: a completion commit whose subject is literally `@` is a wrapper placeholder mid-amend.** It is not a malformed delivery and it is not something to grade — it means the chain has not finished. `ee44b773` on `task-2f554e29` shows the same shape one commit earlier (`a6d1a882  commit: @` → `ee44b773  commit (amend)`), so this is the wrapper's normal behaviour rather than an incident here.

**Amending is a hand-landing habit, not wrapper behaviour.** I generalised from two rows that happened to share a delivery method, and I named the wrong actor.

`@ feat(task-77af2cd3): extract the curated policy root barrel below the 400-line cap` — a **stray leading `@ `** that the final amend strips. **The reflog prints `commit: @` because it shows the subject only up to the first space.** I read the reflog's truncated subject and reported it as the commit's, which is how "placeholder whose subject is literally `@`" got into a durable record.

